Key Vault across regions

Compare regional recovery options for secrets, certificates, and keys. Start with regional behavior, then choose a pattern that your workload's services support.

Design preview - October 27 update. This is a proposed layout, not published guidance. Scenario statuses and service-specific recommendations remain subject to validation. The current guide and PDF are unchanged.

Paired and nonpaired regions

Region pairing is a service-specific recovery relationship, not an application disaster-recovery plan. Check whether your chosen regions support the replication behavior you need.

Paired regions

Where eligible, Standard and Premium vaults replicate asynchronously to a Microsoft-managed copy in the paired region.

Microsoft controls failover. Access is read-only after failover; your workload must tolerate the recovery timing and operation restrictions.

Nonpaired regions

Do not assume a Microsoft-managed secondary vault exists. Design recovery explicitly with independent regional vaults or supported Managed HSM replication.

Validate service support, geography, private connectivity, identities, and key access in the recovery region.

Check regional exceptions: no pair (3+0), asymmetric pairing (3+1), and pairs outside the geography. Pairing alone does not establish a data-residency boundary.

Endpoint timing, failover eligibility, and read-only restrictions will be qualified against current Microsoft documentation in the final guide.

Secrets and certificates

Secrets and certificates - Pattern 1: Key Vault in each region

  • Deployment: Vault per workload per region.
  • Artifact origin: Deployment pipeline.
  • Distribution: Customer-controlled rollout.
  • During an outage: Full local read and write.
  • Watch for: Keep secrets and certificates synchronized; roll out changes sequentially.

Secrets and certificates - Pattern 2: Key Vault in a paired region

  • Deployment: One vault and its paired-region copy.
  • Artifact origin: Deployment pipeline.
  • Distribution: Microsoft-managed replication.
  • During an outage: Read-only after failover.
  • Watch for: Requires an eligible same-geography pair; accept Microsoft-managed recovery timing.

Keys - Pattern 1: Standard vault with paired-region replication

  • Deployment: One Standard vault.
  • Artifact origin: Key created in primary vault.
  • Distribution: Microsoft-managed replication.
  • During an outage: Read-only after failover.
  • Watch for: Software-protected keys. Validate recovery timing and consuming-service requirements.

Keys - Pattern 2: Premium vault with paired-region replication

  • Deployment: One Premium vault.
  • Artifact origin: Key created in primary vault.
  • Distribution: Microsoft-managed replication.
  • During an outage: Read-only after failover.
  • Watch for: HSM-protected keys. Validate recovery timing and consuming-service requirements.

Keys - Pattern 3: Key Vault in each region

  • Deployment: Standard or Premium vault per region.
  • Artifact origin: Different key in each vault.
  • Distribution: Independent regional vaults.
  • During an outage: Full local read and write.
  • Watch for: Use only when the consuming service permits independent regional keys and vaults.

Keys - Pattern 4: Premium vaults with external HSM / BYOK

  • Deployment: Premium vault per region.
  • Artifact origin: Customer-owned external HSM.
  • Distribution: BYOK import into each vault.
  • During an outage: Full local read and write.
  • Watch for: Import and rotate keys in each vault; independent-vault service restrictions still apply.

Keys - Pattern 5: Managed HSM with geo-replication

  • Deployment: Primary and one extended region.
  • Artifact origin: Key created in Managed HSM.
  • Distribution: Managed HSM geo-replication.
  • During an outage: Read and write in healthy region.
  • Watch for: Asynchronous replication: recent key and role changes may be lost if the primary is unrecoverable.

Keys - Pattern 6: Managed HSM geo-replication with external HSM / BYOK

  • Deployment: Primary and one extended region.
  • Artifact origin: Customer-owned external HSM.
  • Distribution: BYOK import, then geo-replication.
  • During an outage: Read and write in healthy region.
  • Watch for: Same replication window as Keys - Pattern 5, with external key origin and an import process.

Keys - Pattern 7: Managed HSM with external key management

  • Deployment: Managed HSM and EKM proxy.
  • Artifact origin: Customer-owned external HSM.
  • Distribution: Key reference; no key replication.
  • During an outage: Depends on failed component.
  • Watch for: Key material stays outside Microsoft. No geo-replication or end-to-end SLA; verify each service integration.

Application-level encryption

Choose by application requirements

Confirm the cryptographic operations and SDK your application uses. Separate key ownership, HSM protection, and recovery objectives from the choice of regional topology.

Final section: verified service conditions, recovery implications, and a direct Microsoft reference.

Azure Storage GRS

A shared key dependency spans both data copies

The source distinguishes a shared vault/key from independent regional vaults. Explain the common dependency, Microsoft-managed recovery conditions, and supported Managed HSM or EKM integration before recommending a pattern.

Final section: verified service conditions, recovery implications, and a direct Microsoft reference.

Storage object replication

Independent accounts can have independent key dependencies

Describe source and destination account encryption separately. Validate the selected key-store integration and replication configuration rather than carrying GRS restrictions into object replication.

Final section: verified service conditions, recovery implications, and a direct Microsoft reference.

VM disk encryption

Name the encryption feature precisely

Distinguish managed-disk server-side encryption using Disk Encryption Sets from Azure Disk Encryption. Show the source and recovery region key dependencies for the chosen feature.

Final section: verified service conditions, recovery implications, and a direct Microsoft reference.

Azure Site Recovery

Check the complete replication path

Cover the source Disk Encryption Set, cache storage account, target Disk Encryption Set, identities, and regional keys. The source selects Keys - Pattern 3; exact restrictions and BYOK cases still need validation.

Final section: verified service conditions, recovery implications, and a direct Microsoft reference.

PostgreSQL / MySQL Flexible Server

Keep PostgreSQL and MySQL conditions separate

Confirm the feature is geo-redundant backup, geo-restore, or replica-based recovery. Product-level CMK support is not sufficient evidence for every recovery mode.

Final section: verified service conditions, recovery implications, and a direct Microsoft reference.

SQL / Cosmos DB geo-replication

Validate key access, endpoint continuity, and rotation

The source favors replicated Managed HSM and describes Microsoft-managed vault recovery as an alternative. Check SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, and Cosmos DB independently, including rotation requirements.

Final section: verified service conditions, recovery implications, and a direct Microsoft reference.

Database geo-restore

Resolve the cross-geography restriction

The source's geo-restore description and support cells conflict. Identify the specific service, region combination, key location, and restore operation before assigning support statuses.

Final section: verified service conditions, recovery implications, and a direct Microsoft reference.

Purview Information Protection

Identify the exact Microsoft 365 encryption feature

Separate Information Protection tenant keys from Microsoft 365 Customer Key. Explain the long-lived decryption dependency, key preservation, and recovery design without assuming all Managed HSM integrations also support EKM.

Final section: verified service conditions, recovery implications, and a direct Microsoft reference.
